name: Fig
overview: The fig holds significant cultural and practical importance in Scripture, symbolizing both human vulnerability and God's provision. After the fall, Adam and Eve used fig leaves to cover their nakedness, illustrating an early recognition of sin and shame (Genesis 3:7). Figs were common in the Promised Land and Egypt, valued not only as fruit but also preserved as cakes, such as those Abigail sent to David in a gesture of peace and provision (1 Samuel 25:18). The presence of fig trees alongside other fruitful crops highlights the land's abundance and God's blessing (Deuteronomy 8:8), while their use in trade and remedy underscores their everyday significance in biblical life.
